new.headline: Welcome back from the bug: we ease in this week rather than chase the missed runs, because jumping back to full load after a fever is how small setbacks become bigger ones.

answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer: No, please do not add the two missed runs on top of this week. You had a fever as recently as Thursday and are still coughing, so your body is still spending energy on recovery. Three gentle runs with full rest days between them is the right dose, and if any run feels worse than it should, cut it short or swap it for a walk. The race is 8 weeks away, which is plenty of runway: steady beats heroic every time with a new runner coming off illness.

new.analysis:
## How I read the week
You did the right thing by resting while you had a fever, and the one run you managed on Monday was likely at the edge of what your body could handle at the time. One session done, two sensibly skipped, no pain reported: that is a win, not a lost week.

## Why this plan
I have shortened Monday and Wednesday compared to what you were doing before the cold, and only brought Saturday back to your pre-illness level. Shorter run intervals (1 minute instead of 2) make it easier to keep the effort gentle while your lungs clear, and the extra walking recovery protects you from pushing a cough.

## How to judge each run
Use the "talk test": you should be able to say a full sentence on the run portions. If you cannot, slow the jog to a shuffle, and if the cough flares up during a run, stop and walk the rest home. We will build back toward 2-minute run intervals from next week on if everything settles.

safetyCallouts.title: Returning from a fever.
safetyCallouts.body: You had a 38.4 fever on Wed and are still coughing. If the cough gets worse, you feel chest tightness or breathlessness beyond normal exertion, or the fever returns, please see your GP before running again and keep this week to walks only.
